messages.content: You are the DIA designation-desk decision agent. Your remit is to assess center-designation matters against Departmental issuances, interagency coordination records, and the status of required approvals, then state DIA’s disposition in the working record. Follow applicable DoD directives and the DIA records schedule; preserve source language when a document is controlling, and distinguish recorded facts from staff assessments. The Departmental action office maintains directive text; the Under Secretary’s staff maintains approval routing; the DIA plans desk maintains organizational submissions. Tools: records.search retrieves indexed directives, memoranda, and prior action files. comms.send posts a message to an office channel. log.write appends a dated entry to the designation record. Before a consequential action, the Benchbook harness may place the closest past case from its casebook in your context as reference material to weigh, not an order.

messages.name: records.search
messages.content:
CENTER PROFILE EXTRACT — AFMIC
Record class: organization profile / coordination copy

Organization field: AFMIC is DIA’s Armed Forces Medical Intelligence Center. The profile’s header was refreshed after the annual directory check; the footer still points to an older intranet address.

Production field: In the federal system, AFMIC is the principal producer of medical intelligence. The profile describes its products as finished assessments built from all-source reporting. Listed subject lines include infectious-disease threats, the condition of medical services, environmental hazards affecting health, and medical science and technology. The list is followed by a note that finished items are distributed to the customer set named on each report.

Role field: the center functions as a national intelligence center. The entry is not labeled as a proposed future role; it appears in the current profile section alongside its production responsibilities.

Coordination field: AFMIC works with U.S. domestic agencies on protection of homeland health. This entry is carried under external partnerships, not under the internal staffing chart. The profile does not provide partner counts in this extract.

Routine annotations: the directory office asked that legacy hyperlinks be checked before the next annual refresh. A separate note records that the training-room projector was returned to the supply cage. The profile’s format conversion inserted a blank line between the production and coordination fields; no substantive edits are recorded in the conversion log.
